title: HRIS / HCM migration
summary: Moving the employee system of record (for example Workday to Rippling). The HRIS feeds payroll, benefits, identity, finance, and compliance, so cutover dates are driven by payroll and benefit calendars, not by technical readiness.

items.name: I-9 and personnel files
drivers: high-risk integration type (Compliance records (I-9, personnel files))
checks: I-9 and personnel file retention requirements confirmed with Legal
Audit trail and document images migrated or archived with access
Legacy system retained read-only for the retention period

drivers: dated constraint: Payroll run on the 15th and last day
checks: Parallel payroll runs reconciled to the penny before go-live
Cutover at a quarter boundary (ideally year start) to simplify YTD balances and tax filings

needs_decision.name: Legacy bonus tool
needs_decision.why: No target support: replace, retire, or build a workaround (record as an ADR)

gotchas.title: Position-based versus job-based models
gotchas.detail: If Workday position management is in use, the target job-based model needs a deliberate mapping of positions, requisitions, and headcount plans.

gotchas.title: Integration Cloud replacements
gotchas.detail: EIBs, Core Connectors, and Studio integrations must each map to a target connector, API, or file feed. Inventory by system and by owner, and expect orphans.

gotchas.title: Calculated fields and custom reports
gotchas.detail: Workday calculated fields and composite reports used by Finance and HR have no direct equivalent. Rebuild against target reporting and reconcile headcount to the old numbers.

gotchas.title: Workday as IdP provisioning hub
gotchas.detail: If Workday drives joiners and leavers into the IdP, the handoff to the new HR source must be tested before it replaces the feed.

gotchas.title: Cutover dates belong to payroll, not IT
gotchas.detail: A mid-quarter or mid-year payroll move forces year-to-date wage imports and complicates tax filings. Anchor the schedule on a quarter or year boundary and work backward.

gotchas.title: Effective-dated history
gotchas.detail: Source systems keep dated job, comp, and org history. Decide how much history is imported versus archived, and keep the source read-only for lookups and audits.

gotchas.title: Worker ID continuity
gotchas.detail: Downstream systems key on employee ID. Keep a source-to-target mapping table and test every consumer against it.

gotchas.title: Benefits carriers have their own calendars
gotchas.detail: Carrier file changes take weeks to validate, and open enrollment timing may forbid changes. Start carrier testing at project kickoff.

gotchas.title: Business processes and security roles do not port
gotchas.detail: Approval chains, delegations, and role-based data access (especially compensation) must be rebuilt and access-reviewed. Over-permissioned defaults are a common leak.

gotchas.title: Compliance retention outlives the contract
gotchas.detail: I-9 and personnel records have statutory retention periods. Confirm the archive keeps them reachable after the old subscription ends.

gotchas.title: Ownership overlap with IT products
gotchas.detail: Some HRIS vendors also sell identity and device management. Decide explicitly whether to adopt them or keep your IdP and MDM, so ownership is not ambiguous.

gotchas.title: Verify vendor behavior
gotchas.detail: Integration catalogs and payroll coverage change by release and state. Confirm every Critical and High item with the vendor in writing.

discovery: Workday: list all integration systems (EIBs, Core Connectors, Studio) with schedules and owners from the integrations report
Workday: export custom reports and calculated fields with last-run date and audience
Workday: export business process definitions and security groups with membership
Payroll: calendar of pay periods, tax filing dates, and year-end processing
Benefits: carrier list, file formats, plan year dates, open enrollment window
Finance: GL mapping, cost center list, and recurring HR-driven reports
Ask IT for every system that consumes employee data (IdP, ATS, LMS, expense, Slack)

phases.name: Discover and decide
activities: Inventory every consumer of employee data
Fix cutover quarter with Payroll and Finance
Decide history depth and archive approach

phases.name: Build and map
activities: Configure org, jobs, comp, and security in the target
Build data mapping and ID continuity table
Rebuild integrations and reports in the target

phases.name: Validate and parallel run
activities: Run parallel payroll cycles until clean
Validate carrier files and accounting journals

phases.name: Cut over and stabilize
activities: Execute cutover on the agreed boundary
Hypercare through first full pay cycle and first close
Archive source and complete access review

cutover_checklist: Payroll sign-off from two parallel runs with zero unexplained variance
Open transactions and approvals drained in the source
Source system frozen to changes at an agreed time
Downstream feeds switched in dependency order
Security roles and compensation access reviewed
rollback: Before the point of no return (first live payroll), the source remains system of record and the target load is discarded
After first live payroll, rollback is a forward fix: define the manual payroll fallback and who authorizes it
Integrations: keep source feeds ready to re-enable for each consumer
exit_criteria: Two clean live pay cycles and one clean accounting close
All consumers receive data from the new source
Carrier reconciliations clean for one billing cycle
Source system archived read-only with documented retention owner

decisions.title: Adopt vendor IT products or keep existing IdP and MDM
